## Channel positioning

Handle:
@sportenvopadel

Website:
https://sportenvo.com/

Entity line used consistently in descriptions:
SPORTENVO — Commercial Padel Court Systems & Project Solutions.

Contact:
sales@sportenvo.com

## Publishing principle

Use real SPORTENVO court, factory, installation and project footage. Avoid generic AI visuals, unrelated stock clips and exaggerated weather scenes. The goal is to answer a buyer question clearly, then show real technical or project evidence.

Recommended long-form format:
- 2.5–5 minutes
- 16:9
- 1080p or higher
- English narration or clear English subtitles
- first answer within 10 seconds
- one primary search intent per video
- chapters for videos over ~2 minutes
- one matching guide + one matching product page + one project enquiry link in description

Do not stuff tags or repeat the same keyword unnaturally.

# VIDEO 01 — ROOF

## Search intent

Primary:
- padel court roof
- retractable padel court roof
- fixed vs retractable padel roof

Secondary:
- aluminum alloy padel roof
- commercial padel court roof
- padel court canopy

## Title

Padel Court Roof Systems: Fixed vs Retractable for Commercial Projects

Alternative title for later test:
Fixed vs Retractable Padel Court Roof: What Clubs Should Compare

## Thumbnail text

FIXED vs RETRACTABLE

Use:
- real roof open/closed images
- no extra marketing badges
- SPORTENVO logo small
- clear structural view

## Opening hook — 0:00–0:12

Voiceover:
"Should a commercial padel club use a fixed roof or a retractable roof? The answer depends on clear height, span, wind, drainage, foundation reactions, operating needs and budget — not only the roof appearance."

Visual:
Real fixed roof / retractable open / retractable closed cuts.

## Structure

0:00 — Fixed vs retractable: quick answer  
0:20 — What a fixed roof is best for  
0:55 — What a retractable roof is best for  
1:35 — Clear height and span  
2:05 — Wind, drainage and foundation interfaces  
2:45 — Questions to send before quotation  
3:15 — SPORTENVO project support / CTA

## Core talking points

Fixed roof:
- permanent weather protection
- simpler operating concept
- suitable for long-term commercial facilities

Retractable roof:
- open / covered operating flexibility
- project-specific aluminum-alloy configuration
- requires review of movement, controls, wind, drainage and foundation interfaces

Buyer checklist:
- country / city
- court quantity
- site dimensions
- preferred clear height
- wind conditions
- foundation status
- drainage constraints
- fixed or retractable preference

Guardrail:
There is no universal roof specification for every site. Final structural design and approvals remain project-specific.

## Description

A commercial padel court roof should be selected around the venue, not just the appearance.

In this video, SPORTENVO compares fixed and retractable padel court roof systems and explains the project interfaces buyers should review: clear height, span, wind, drainage, foundation reactions, operation and local engineering requirements.

## Title

Mobile Padel Court: Site Preparation, Foundation & Relocation Explained

Alternative title:
Portable Padel Court: What Buyers Should Know Before Installation

## Thumbnail text

MOBILE PADEL COURT

Subline only if visually clean:
SITE · BASE · RELOCATION

## Opening hook — 0:00–0:12

Voiceover:
"A mobile padel court can reduce dependence on permanent civil work and support future relocation, but mobile does not mean zero site preparation."

Visual:
Real Mobile court + base detail + Harwich project.

## Structure

0:00 — What a Mobile Padel Court is  
0:30 — Mobile vs portable vs relocatable terminology  
0:55 — Site and ground requirements  
1:35 — Modular foundation concept  
2:05 — How future relocation works

## Core talking points

- SPORTENVO official product name: Mobile Padel Court
- portable / relocatable are common buyer search terms
- suitable ground is still required
- drainage and level review remain required
- anchoring and local requirements remain project-specific
- relocation depends on dismantling, packing, transport and the future receiving site

Do not claim:
- no groundwork for every project
- suitable for any surface without assessment
- guaranteed relocation without re-review

## Description

What is a Mobile Padel Court — and is it the same as a portable or relocatable padel court?

SPORTENVO uses Mobile Padel Court as the official product-series name. The system is planned to reduce dependence on permanent civil work and support future relocation, while still requiring review of ground conditions, level, drainage, anchoring, access and local requirements.

# VIDEO 03 — FOUNDATION

## Search intent

Primary:
- padel court foundation
- padel court concrete foundation
- modular padel court foundation

Secondary:
- does a padel court need concrete
- padel court base
- steel foundation padel court

## Title

Padel Court Foundation: Concrete vs Modular Steel Base

Alternative title:
Does a Padel Court Need Concrete? Concrete vs Modular Foundation

## Thumbnail text

CONCRETE vs MODULAR

## Opening hook — 0:00–0:12

Voiceover:
"Does every padel court need a full concrete foundation? Not necessarily. But every court still needs a foundation strategy that resolves ground support, level, drainage, anchoring and structural loads."

Visual:
Concrete/site preparation → modular base → installed court.

## Structure

0:00 — Quick answer  
0:25 — What the foundation must do  
0:55 — Traditional concrete base  
1:30 — Modular steel foundation  
2:10 — Ground, drainage and anchoring  
2:45 — Roof and wind interfaces  
3:15 — Which site information to send

## Core talking points

Foundation must address:
- stable level support
- structural loads
- anchoring
- drainage
- ground conditions
- wind exposure
- court type
- roof reactions where applicable
- local engineering requirements

Concrete:
- common for permanent commercial installations
- coordinated civil work and drainage

Modular:
- can reduce dependence on full concrete construction for suitable projects
- relevant to leased / flexible / relocatable sites
- still requires site preparation and engineering review

## Description

A padel court foundation is more than a flat surface. It must coordinate the court loads, anchoring, ground support, level tolerances and drainage with the actual site.

This video compares traditional concrete civil work with a modular steel foundation approach and explains when each option may be appropriate.

# Measurement

Track in GA4:
- sessions from source = youtube
- landing page
- start_project_click
- start_project_view
- project_form_submit
- generate_lead

Use campaign names exactly:
- roof-fixed-vs-retractable
- mobile-padel-explained
- foundation-concrete-vs-modular

After 14–28 days compare:
- YouTube impressions
- CTR
- average view duration
- search terms
- website referral sessions
- start-project rate
- generated leads

Do not judge a video only by views. A small number of highly relevant commercial viewers can be more valuable than broad consumer traffic.
